sections.h2: Where the Hardin County Clerk is and what it holds
sections.html:
The clerk works from Suite 103 of the Hardin County Government Building, 150 N. Provident Way, Elizabethtown, KY 42701, phone 270-765-2171. Doors are open weekdays from 7:45 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon. A branch at 101 W. Lincoln Trail Blvd in Radcliff handles vehicle registrations Tuesday through Thursday from 8 to 4, but deeds go to Elizabethtown.

This office keeps deeds, mortgages, wills, plats, liens, assumed names and marriage records, and it also issues vehicle titles and tags and runs elections. A seller meets it three ways: when the deed to the buyer is recorded, when an old mortgage needs a release of record, and when a bill that missed the sheriff's April 15 cutoff has moved to the clerk.

Courthouse fires in 1864 and 1932 destroyed county records, so a title examiner working on a very old chain may find gaps that predate the present 1934 courthouse.

The clerk's website runs an eSearch name search that works as a guest, and it indexes far more than deeds. Index types include deeds, mortgages, deeds of release, affidavits of descent, plats, powers of attorney, restrictions, wills, lis pendens, mechanics liens and ad valorem liens, along with fiscal court minutes and ordinances.

Two searches pay off before listing. A search on your own name should show the mortgage and, once paid, a deed of release. A search for liens should show nothing left unreleased, since a lien filed against a prior owner or a contractor can surface at a title company in the final week.

sections.h2: What a deed must contain to be accepted
sections.html:
The clerk must turn away a deed that breaks a content rule in KRS 382.135 or KRS 382.110. Title attorneys handle these items routinely, but a family transfer written from a form is where gaps show up.

  • Full names and mailing addresses for both parties.
  • The full price, backed by a notarized certificate signed by both sides. A gift deed carries a certificate saying so, with an estimated fair cash value.
  • An in-care-of address for the bill of the year of transfer.
  • The source of the grantor's title, by deed book and page when it came from a recorded deed, or a plain explanation when it came by inheritance.

An estate that passes land by will or intestacy adds one more filing: the personal representative lodges an affidavit listing who received each parcel and what it was valued at.

The clerk posts a fee schedule alongside its formatting rules. Paper should be white and unbound, in black ink, with no seals or highlighter and a three inch blank strip across the top of page one. Electronic filers use Simplifile, ePn or CSC.

Sample Hardin County Clerk recording charges
DocumentCharge
Deed or easement$50.00
Mortgage$80.00
Release of mortgage, full or partial$46.00
Affidavit of descent and distribution$50.00
Power of attorney$50.00
Plat filing$50.00
Will$47.00
Certified copy$5.00

Most documents add $3.00 for every page past five and $4.00 per extra reference, and a mortgage adds $3.00 per page past thirty. Confirm the total with the clerk before mailing a packet.

sections.h2: Transfer tax owed by the seller
sections.html:
The grantor pays fifty cents per $500 block of value, with any leftover amount counted as a full block, under KRS 142.050. The clerk works the figure out from the value stated in the deed, collects it before accepting the paper, and certifies the payment date and amount on the deed itself. The tax is collected once per transaction, in whichever county the deed is filed. The clerk keeps 5 percent for the work, and the rest goes to the county treasurer every three months for the general fund.

Exemptions include foreclosure deeds, deeds in lieu, transfers between spouses in a divorce, partitions, and parent to child gifts with only nominal consideration. When a deed carries no stated price, the tax is figured on the open market estimate.

sections.h2: When a deed is rejected or filed late
sections.html:
The statute bars the clerk from lodging a deed that fails the content rules, so a rejected package usually means a corrected deed, a new notarization and a second trip. A deed recorded in error still counts as notice to later buyers and creditors, but the defect can draw questions from a title insurer.

Timing rules apply to some transfers. A lender that takes a deed in lieu of foreclosure must file it with the clerk within 45 days of signing. A grantee under a deed from a court-appointed commissioner has five business days from receipt to file. If you are the seller on either kind of transfer, confirm with the other side that the deed has been filed before you consider the matter closed.

sections.h2: Other filings a seller may need
sections.html:
Selling often trips over small filings. These come up most often, with the clerk's charges.

  • Release of a paid mortgage: $46.00.
  • Affidavit of descent and distribution after an inheritance: $50.00.
  • Power of attorney: $50.00, and a revocation: $46.00.
  • Release of a mechanics lien: $46.00, or $60.00 for a bond that releases it.
  • Release of a judgment lien or federal tax lien: $46.00. A state tax lien release costs $5.00.
  • City lien and city release: $23.00.
  • Notary service at the counter: $5.00 per acknowledgement plus $2.00 per notarization.

None of these replaces a title search, but ordering them early prevents the delay of a lender waiting on a release.

sections.h2: Unpaid property tax and the clerk
sections.html:
Sellers with a delinquent bill from a prior year get the payoff from the clerk. After April 15 a bill is a certificate of delinquency in the clerk's office, and the clerk's page offers a delinquent tax calculator and tax sale information. The recording schedule also lists $30.00 to record a certificate assignment and $46.00 for a reassignment or release.

Request a payoff in writing, dated near the closing date, because interest accrues monthly. If a third party bought the certificate, the payoff goes to that buyer. The closing agent can pay it from the sale proceeds, and a cash buyer who closes quickly leaves less time for interest to grow.

Hardin County has 44,622 households averaging 2.44 people each, and median gross rent is $971. With Fort Knox in the county, some sellers and buyers work to a fixed report date, so a deed that meets every content rule on the first attempt avoids a trip back to Suite 103.

Before closing day, call 270-765-2171 and ask what the clerk will need from your side: the signed deed, the notarized price certificate, the payoff or release for any mortgage, and the money for transfer tax and recording. Having each piece ready the day before keeps a closing from stalling at the counter, and it gives you time to fix a missing signature or address.

faqs.q: Can a deed be e-recorded in Hardin County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: Yes. The Hardin County Clerk lists Simplifile, ePn and CSC as accepted electronic recording vendors.

faqs.q: How much is a mortgage release at the Hardin County Clerk?
faqs.a: $46.00 for a full or partial release, plus $3.00 for each page past five. The deed itself is $50.00.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Hardin County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, at fifty cents per $500 block of value, paid when the deed is filed. A leftover amount counts as a full block.

faqs.q: Does the Radcliff branch record deeds?
faqs.a: No. The Radcliff branch at 101 W. Lincoln Trail Blvd handles vehicle registration on Tuesday through Thursday. Deeds are recorded at Suite 103, 150 N. Provident Way, Elizabethtown.

faqs.q: Is a state tax lien release cheaper than a federal one in Hardin County?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk charges $5.00 to record a state tax lien or its release and $46.00 for a federal tax lien or release.
